title: High-Salt Binding Buffer Reduces DnaK Co-Elution During Nickel Affinity Purification of a Recombinant Collagen-Like Protein
research_question: Does increasing NaCl from 300 to 500 mM reduce DnaK co-elution during Ni-NTA purification of His10-ColX3 without a major loss of target recovery?
key_findings: 500 mM NaCl reduced the DnaK-to-ColX3 ratio 2.7-fold | ColX3 recovery decreased modestly from 5.6 to 5.1 mg/L | ATP/Mg2+ did not improve purity beyond high salt alone
critical_negations: ATP-Mg2+ did not further improve purity | DnaK was not completely removed | DnaK phosphorylation was not measured
forbidden_claims: The target protein was DnaK | High salt increased ColX3 yield | ATP completely removed DnaK | DnaK phosphorylation caused the effect | Size-exclusion chromatography was used

title: A Transient Alkaline Shift Reversibly Increases Association of the Chaperone ChpA with Heat-Damaged Lysozyme
research_question: Does a transient alkaline shift reversibly increase ChpA binding to heat-damaged lysozyme?
key_findings: Binding increased 3.2-fold at pH 8.5 | Binding returned to 1.1-fold after 20 min at pH 7.2 | Total ChpA changed by less than 6%
critical_negations: Phosphorylation was not assessed | Total ChpA did not materially increase | Native lysozyme showed low binding
forbidden_claims: ChpA phosphorylation caused binding | ChpA expression increased 3.2-fold | The effect was irreversible | Surface plasmon resonance was used

title: Scale-Up of Soluble PhaZ Hydrolase Production from 2-L to 30-L Fermentation Using Fixed Aeration and Agitation
research_question: How does fixed-setting scale-up from 2 L to 30 L affect biomass, soluble PhaZ production, insoluble product, acetate, and enzyme quality?
key_findings: Biomass increased at 30 L | Soluble PhaZ decreased from 8.2 to 6.3 mg/L | Insoluble PhaZ increased from 34% to 57% | Acetate increased from 1.1 to 3.8 g/L | Specific activity was unchanged
critical_negations: Dissolved oxygen was not measured at 30 L | kLa was not calculated | Specific activity did not decrease materially
forbidden_claims: Oxygen limitation was directly proven | The 30-L process increased soluble PhaZ | Specific activity doubled | A DO cascade was used at 30 L

title: MpxR Cleaves a Periplasmic Fluorescent Reporter Independently of the Canonical Heat-Shock Regulators
research_question: Does MpxR cleave a periplasmic reporter, and is cleavage dependent on DnaK, DnaJ, sigma32, or FtsH?
key_findings: Wild-type MpxR increased cleavage 4.6-fold | Ser201Ala was inactive | DnaK, DnaJ, sigma32, and FtsH depletion did not materially reduce cleavage
critical_negations: The heat-shock regulators were not required | No phosphorylation assay was performed | The paper is not primarily about DnaK or sigma32
forbidden_claims: The study characterized DnaK phosphorylation | FtsH was the protease that cleaved the reporter | sigma32 activated MpxR | Surface plasmon resonance was used | The paper is a heat-shock review

title: Trehalose Preserves Soluble LmOx During Repeated Freeze-Thaw Cycles Without Increasing Catalytic Turnover
research_question: Does trehalose preserve soluble LmOx during repeated freeze-thaw cycles, and does it change specific activity?
key_findings: 10% trehalose preserved 84% soluble LmOx versus 41% without trehalose | Specific activity remained 118-123 U/mg and did not increase | 10% was the lowest concentration at the recovery plateau
critical_negations: Specific activity did not increase | Sucrose was not tested | pH 6.0 was not tested | 30 C thawing was not tested
forbidden_claims: Trehalose activated LmOx | Sucrose was superior to trehalose | The experiment was performed at pH 6.0 | Samples were thawed at 30 C | 20% trehalose doubled turnover

title: Co-Expression of PdxJ Increases Soluble EnzQ Production Without Detectable Binding to Purified EnzQ
research_question: Does PdxJ co-expression increase soluble EnzQ, and do purified PdxJ and EnzQ form a stable complex?
key_findings: Soluble EnzQ increased from 2.4 to 7.1 mg/L | Total expression increased only 1.2-fold | No stable binding was detected by three assays
critical_negations: No stable complex was detected | A transient interaction was not demonstrated | Total expression did not increase threefold
forbidden_claims: PdxJ binds EnzQ with high affinity | SEC demonstrated a PdxJ-EnzQ complex | MST measured a finite Kd | PdxJ increased total expression threefold

title: Low-Temperature Induction Reduces Inclusion-Body Formation of SynLig-B Without Changing Total Expression
research_question: Does low-temperature induction improve SynLig-B solubility, and is the improvement due to greater total expression?
key_findings: Soluble fraction increased from 18% to 57% | Soluble yield increased from 1.9 to 5.8 mg/L | Total expression remained about 10 mg/L
critical_negations: Total expression did not increase | Apparent molecular mass did not change | Temperature and duration both changed
forbidden_claims: Total SynLig-B expression tripled | The 16 C sample was induced for 6 h | DnaK binding was measured | The molecular mass decreased

title: Batch-Binding Time from 5 to 60 Minutes Does Not Limit Capture of His-CasP from Clarified Lysate
research_question: Does extending Ni-resin batch-binding time from 5 to 60 min improve His-CasP capture, and is resin capacity a separate limitation?
key_findings: Bound recovery was 73-75% at all standard binding times | Extending time did not improve capture | Low resin reduced recovery to 38% and increased flow-through to 45%
critical_negations: Longer binding did not improve recovery | The study did not test less than 5 min | The low-resin result should not be attributed to short contact time
forbidden_claims: 60 min gave the highest meaningful recovery | Binding kinetics required one hour | The low-resin group used 5 min | Phosphate incorporation was measured

title: ATP Selectively Releases ClpH, but Not GroX, from a Heat-Damaged Casein Matrix
research_question: Do ClpH and GroX differ in ATP-Mg2+-dependent release from a heat-damaged casein matrix?
key_findings: ATP-Mg2+ released 81% of ClpH but 7% of GroX | ADP-Mg2+ released 19% of ClpH | ATP without MgCl2 released 24% of ClpH | GroX required acid elution
critical_negations: No phosphorylation assay was performed | ATP alone was insufficient for efficient release | GroX was not released efficiently by ATP-Mg2+
forbidden_claims: ClpH was phosphorylated | GroX was released by ATP | ATP-Mg2+ prevented both proteins from binding | Surface plasmon resonance was used | A kinase mediated release
